stage.title: Welcome to the Build room! 🏗️
stage.text: This is where your game's world gets made. This little tour points at each part — click Next to walk through, or Skip if you already know your way.

stage.title: The world
stage.text: This is your level, live. Drag empty space to orbit around it, right-drag to slide, scroll to zoom. Everything you make ends up in here.

stage.title: Put things in it
stage.text: These buttons drop things into the world — boxes, sprites, and the invisible helpers: Trigger (something happens when the player walks in), Spawn, Checkpoint, Kill. The Toy Chest room has even more to drag in.

stage.title: The Behavior Shelf 🪙
stage.text: Ready-made game pieces that already work: coins, enemies, doors, moving platforms. Click one to drop it in — then change anything about it. Its rules live in the Rule Cards room if you want to see how it thinks.

stage.title: Move things around
stage.text: Click a thing in the world, then use these three: the first slides it, the second turns it, the third resizes it. Grab the colored arrows and rings right on the object.

stage.title: The ground
stage.text: Add ground here, pick its texture, then hit Paint & Sculpt — a gold ring follows your mouse. Drag to raise hills, dig dips, or paint textures. Keys 1, 2, 3 switch what you're painting with.

stage.title: Light & shadows
stage.text: Pick your shadow style — Blob is fast and cartoony, the soft ones look real. Slide the sun around for morning or evening light, and Bounce makes everything glow a little warmer.

stage.title: Your scenes
stage.text: A game can have many levels — they're listed here. Everything you place belongs to the scene you're in.

stage.title: Try it! ▶
stage.text: The most important button in the whole studio. Press Play and your level runs right here — jump around, see what feels good, press Stop, fix, Play again. Great games are made by playing them every few minutes.

atelier.title: The art table 🎨
atelier.text: Draw images for your game — or edit ones you bring in. Quick walk-through?

atelier.title: Layers
atelier.text: Clear plastic sheets stacked up. Draw the body on one, the face on another — fix one without wrecking the other. The checkbox hides a sheet, the slider makes it see-through.

atelier.title: The tools
atelier.text: Draw and Erase are pencil and rubber. Fill pours color into a shape. Line and Box drag corner to corner. Pick steals a color you already used. Select draws a dashed box so Blur and Clear only touch what's inside. Mirror doubles your strokes — great for faces.

atelier.title: Getting art out
atelier.text: PNG keeps see-through parts. JPEG doesn't. 'Sprite File' keeps your layers so you can edit later. And Save to Warehouse puts it in the game.

atelier.title: One more trick
atelier.text: Import PNG brings any picture in at its real size. On a tablet, the camera button snaps a photo straight onto the canvas. Your face can be in your game in ten seconds.

materials.title: The Material Maker ✨
materials.text: A material is more than a picture — it's how a surface behaves in light. You build one with sliders, not paint.

materials.title: Diffuse — the color
materials.text: Pick a pattern and two colors to blend through it. This is the material's face.

materials.title: Specular — the shine
materials.text: Where this map is bright, the surface gleams like metal. Where it's dark, it stays matte.

materials.title: Roughness — the dullness
materials.text: Chalk versus wet paint, decided pixel by pixel.

materials.title: Normal — the bumps
materials.text: This one fakes carving: it tilts how light hits each pixel so flat surfaces look grooved. Crank Depth and watch the sphere — the bumps catch the light as it spins.

materials.title: Use it anywhere
materials.text: Save it and it appears in the 3D Shop's palette with a ✨ — paint any part and the whole shader rides along, into the shipped game too.

kitbay.title: The 3D Shop 🏗️
kitbay.text: Build objects out of parts, like snapping bricks together. Quick tour of the machines?

kitbay.title: Parts and linking
kitbay.text: Add a shape and it attaches to whichever part is picked — that's its parent. Move the parent, children ride along. That's how a car works: body first, wheels attached.

kitbay.title: The gizmo
kitbay.text: Click a part in the viewport and grab the arrows to move, rings to rotate, cubes to scale. Click a box a SECOND time to pick one face and put a texture on just that face.

kitbay.title: Tune everything
kitbay.text: Size, position, rotation, color, roughness, metal, glow — and Bevel, which rounds a box's edges. Real things never have perfectly sharp corners, which is why bevel instantly looks better. Modifiers below: Taper squeezes, Twist spirals, Bumpy roughens.

kitbay.title: The texture palette
kitbay.text: Built-in patterns, your own drawings, and ✨ materials from the Material Maker. Click to paint the picked part — or the picked face.

kitbay.title: Save it
kitbay.text: Your prop lands in the Warehouse, ready to drag into the Build room. Spinning parts (wheels!) get their Connection set to 'Spins'.

foundry.title: The sound kitchen 🔊
foundry.text: Every sound here is a recipe of sliders, never a recording — so you can tweak it forever.

foundry.title: Start from a preset
foundry.text: Jump, Coin, Boom... click one and tweak from there. Mutate rolls the dice — great when you're close but not quite.

foundry.title: The dials
foundry.text: Top sliders shape the sound. The power dials polish it: Brightness muffles, Wobble waves, Wah funks, Chorus thickens, Crunch distorts, Echo repeats, Reverb adds room.

foundry.title: Save it
foundry.text: Saved sounds play in your game AND become instruments in the Music room. One sound, two lives.

sfxedit.title: The sound editor ✂️
sfxedit.text: This edits real audio — saved sounds or imported files, even recordings of your voice.

sfxedit.title: Clean Up first
sfxedit.text: Trim Silence chops dead air — do it first on anything recorded. Normalize evens the volume. Louder saturates instead of crackling. Fades smooth the ends.

sfxedit.title: Then get weird
sfxedit.text: Reverb, Echo, Robot, Faster, Slower, Backwards. Every press plays the result instantly, and Undo steps back.

sfxedit.title: Surgery
sfxedit.text: Drag across the waveform to select a piece — Cut removes it, Keep throws away everything else, Quiet silences just that bit. Play plays only your selection so you know you grabbed right.

soundbooth.title: The music room 🎵
soundbooth.text: A song is a grid: each row is a track, each column a moment. Let me show you the desk.

soundbooth.title: Tracks and sounds
soundbooth.text: Pick a track, then click any sound to put it on that track — chip sounds or anything you made. Your own sounds play at different pitches, like a real sampler.

soundbooth.title: Play the keyboard
soundbooth.text: Q through P are notes. The number row above: sharps. The A row below: flats. Z and X change octave. Whatever you play becomes the note you place in the grid.

soundbooth.title: The grid
soundbooth.text: Click cells to place notes. Double-click a cell to split it into two quick notes — drum fills! 2× Double stretches the whole pattern, ½ Halve squeezes it, zoom gets you close.

soundbooth.title: The mixing desk
soundbooth.text: Every track has Volume, Pan, and the effect dials. Turn them WHILE the song loops — changes land on the next pass. That's real mixing.

soundbooth.title: Ship the song
soundbooth.text: Chain patterns into a full song. WAV downloads it as a real audio file you can use anywhere.

rig.title: Characters 🕺
rig.text: Rigged characters have a skeleton inside — move the bones, the skin follows. This bench loads them and teaches them moves.

rig.title: Load one
rig.text: GLB files, or FBX straight from mixamo.com — free characters and thousands of animations. Download 'FBX Binary, With Skin' for the character itself.

rig.title: Teach it moves
rig.text: Click an animation to play it. Import Animations adds moves from other files — Mixamo downloads 'Without Skin' snap right on, because the bones match by name.

rig.title: Keep it or convert it
rig.text: Save to Game stores the character with all its moves. Download as GLB is also a converter: FBX in, one tidy GLB out.

bricks.title: Rule Cards 🧩
bricks.text: Rules read like sentences: WHEN this happens, IF this is true, DO that. That's real game logic — no typing code.

bricks.title: Sheets
bricks.text: Cards live on a sheet attached to a thing in your game. They run top to bottom, like reading. The Behavior Shelf's pieces keep their sheets here — open 'shelf-coin' to see exactly how a coin thinks.

bricks.title: When you're stuck
bricks.text: The Guidebook explains every card with a little playground where you can try it safely. Understanding a card is how you unlock the advanced ones.
